description: The image displays two horizontal bar charts side-by-side, comparing inference times in minutes for different prompting and pruning techniques on two distinct models: Marco-o1-7B (left chart) and QwQ-32B-Preview (right chart). In both charts, the vertical axis represents “Inference Time (minute)” and is scaled linearly from 0 to 7, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.5. The horizontal axis lists the different methods, with the bars arranged in descending order of inference time, from top to bottom. The legend at the bottom of each chart identifies the color coding: green for Baseline, yellow for Fast-Solving Prompt, gray for SFT, orange for DPO, and blue for O1-Pruner. In the Marco-o1-7B chart, the Baseline (green) has the longest inference time at approximately 2.2 minutes, followed by Fast-Solving Prompt (yellow) at about 2.1 minutes, SFT (gray) at 2.1 minutes, DPO (orange) at 1.5 minutes, and O1-Pruner (blue) at 1.1 minutes. In the QwQ-32B-Preview chart, the Baseline (green) has the longest inference time at 6.0 minutes, followed by SFT (gray) at 5.9 minutes, DPO (orange) at 5.7 minutes, Fast-Solving Prompt (yellow) at 5.0 minutes, and O1-Pruner (blue) at 4.0 minutes. The bars are solid-colored and not grouped or stacked; each bar represents a single method’s inference time for its respective model.
